name: Population stability index (PSI)
definition: For the proportions eᵢ of an expected distribution and aᵢ of an actual one over the same bins, PSI is the sum over bins of (aᵢ - eᵢ) × ln(aᵢ / eᵢ). It is 0 when the proportions match, never negative, and symmetric in the two distributions.
citations: Naeem Siddiqi, Credit Risk Scorecards, Wiley, 2006, chapter 8 (the system stability report).
Bilal Yurdakul and Joshua Naranjo, Statistical properties of the population stability index, Journal of Risk Model Validation 14(4), 2020.

call.inputs: two arrays of bin proportions, expected first

properties.says: Swapping expected and actual doesn't change the index.

provenance.why: Issue #9653 names it in the starting list of distance primitives and two-sample statistics. The issue was written after reading one task's winning runs, so that task counts as a source.
provenance.pattern: Check a well-known method against properties its standard definition implies (docs/coder/design/pattern-components.md, Fable step 6).
